fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 is the only selection, but it currently supplies no explicit A_star, compiler matrices, targets, metric transport, or U_r and P_F certificates. Even a finite pass would address only L1; every signed-kernel, DROP, seam, physical-flip, growth, geometry, splice, and carry obstruction remains open.

Proposal 2 is killed as stated. Contractible cell pairs and equal integral homology do not imply selector-preserving equivalence of boundary kernels, Graver bases, or Euclidean residual norms; its proposed homology comparison is therefore below the L1 gate.

Proposal 3 is killed as stated because the monomial configurations and polarization matrices are unspecified, and a two-NAND failure cannot refute L1 generally. Saturation or circuit agreement for one finite serialization would concern only that serialization, while toric quadratic exchange remains untreated.

Proposal 4 is blocked by primitive cover cycles: finite colored covers can have simple cycles of unbounded length, primitive in their incidence kernels. No mechanism removes or charges these cycles, so three four-gate examples cannot support L2's uniform brick-support bound.

Proposal 5 is a valid equivalence warning but not a compiler mechanism or frontier discriminator. The signed-permutation characterization and shear example only prevent invalid metric reasoning; they establish none of L1-L5 or F1-F5.

Proposal 6 is killed algebraically: NAND is not associative, so it cannot serve as multiplication in the associative algebra required by the normalized bar differential. For example, (0 NAND 0) NAND 1 differs from 0 NAND (0 NAND 1), invalidating the claimed bar-complex contraction.

Proposal 7 is killed in its present form because no fixed verifier, alphabet, tile matrix, or Lawrence recursion is specified, and linear tableau flows provide no mechanism against the already observed signed-flow and diagonal-splice attacks. Its three-step toy test would not distinguish those structural failures from an arbitrary incomplete encoding.
evidence: ROADMAP identifies L1 as the current frontier and requires exact depth-1/2/3 full-matrix kernel identities together with honest-affine Graver audits. Proposal 1 alone directly targets formula-dependent wiring through a fixed routing topology and offers a finite exact falsifier.

The Generation-5 verifier found physical-selector flips at squared distance 20 below 17E while all pair-supported channels remained zero. This makes complete physical, pair, normalization, glue, and DROP coordinates mandatory in any Beneš audit.

The G19 and ordered-pair verifiers exhibit exact signed accepting splices despite extensive emitted flow and coherence rows. Thus local routing correctness or Smith-form agreement cannot replace complete signed-kernel and Graver enumeration.

Prior finite shell passes for pair bags, Walsh metrics, and splitter bags produced no composition theorem, while several finite recursions failed growth. No proposed experiment may be promoted to an all-depth or hardness statement.

Arbitrary unimodular row operations preserve kernels but not Euclidean residual norms; arbitrary column operations also alter selector support and Graver geometry. Proposal 1 must therefore separate kernel equivalence from metric preservation and explicitly transport any residual Gram.
